caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 15 of 1977
lawyer:
M.H. Khandker with Abu Backker—For the Appellant
M. Gholam Rabbani with Ranesh Chandra Maitra—For Respondents 1 & 3
parties:
Md. Wasiq Khan ------- Appellant
Vs.
Md. Sabiq Khan ------- Respondent
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J:-These two appeals arise out of a final decree in a suit for partition. 

 2. Plaintiff respondent Nos 1-3 filed the suit for partition of paternal properties on 24.11.69 being T.S. No. 344 of 1969 of the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dacca, later renumbered as T.S. No 56 of 1972 of the Fourth Court of Subordinate Judge, Dacca, and obtained a preliminary decree on contest on 28.2.73. A Pleader Commissioner was appointed by the Court's order dated 18.9.73 to effect partition of the suit properties. By Order No. 77 dated 10.6.75 the learned Sub-ordinate Judge noted that the Pleader Commissioner has submitted his report. He fixed 10.7.75 as the date for filing objection against the report of the Pleader Commissioner. On 10.7.75, the learned Subordinate Judge passed the following order:— 

 "Plaintiff has filed hajira. Parties have not filed any objection against the report of the Commissioner. So the Commissioner's report is accepted. Therefore, ordered that the preliminary decree is made final. Commissioner's report, map, field book, etc. is made part of the decree." 

 3. As against the aforesaid final decree dated 10.7.75, the defendant No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 76 of 1975 on 3.11.75 under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure along with an application for conduction of delay u/s 5 of the Limitation Act, which was opposed by the plaintiff-respondent. By Judgment and order dated 21.5.79 the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the Miscellaneous Case on contest. As against the order of dismissal the defendant No. 1 has preferred F.M.A. Act.318 of 1979. 

 The defendant No 1 has also preferred F.A. No. 15 of 1977 against the aforesaid final decree dated 10.7.75 in T.S. No. 56 of 1979. Both the two appeals have been heard together and will be disposed of by this Judgment. 

 4. Short facts necessary for the disposal of the two appeals are that Late Khan Bahadur Md. Saddiq died in 1965 leaving behind. 4 sons and 2 daughters. Plaintiff No. 1 and defendant Nos 1-3 are the sons of which defendant No. 2 & 3 are the daughters. Partible properties left by the deceased are (1) Schedule A' property, a town property at 62 R. K. Mission Road, Dacca (2) Schedule property also a town property at 61. R.K. Mission Road, Dacca, (3) Schedule 'C' property, also a town property at plot No. 130, Dhanmondi Residential Area and (4) Schedules D and D(i) property, landed property at Mouza Santanapara, P:S. Rupgonj, District Dacca, Plaintiffs claimed 2/5th share in each of Schedules 'A', 93',. 'C', & 'D' properties Defendants. 1-3 filed a joint written statement contesting the suit but at the time of trial defendants 1 & 2 prayed for separate sahams. Defendant No. 1, the appellant, claimed 3/5th share in schedules 'A' and 'B' properties, 1/5th share in schedules 'C' and 'D' properties and 4/15th share in schedule 'D(1)' properties. Defendant No. 2 claimed 1/5th share in ; schedules 'A', 'B', 'C', and .'D' properties and 1/10th share in schedule 'D(1)' properties. He also claimed an enhanced share in the suit properties for loan advanced to his late father. Defendant No. 4 claimed a share of 1/3rd in Schedule 'D (1)' properties. The learned Subordinate Judge apportioned the share of the parties by his Judgment and preliminary decree dated 28.2.73. Plaintiff's share in Schedule 'A', 'B', 'C' & 'D' properties was held to be 2/5th, and in Schedule 'D(1)' properties to be 1/5th. The share of defendant No. 1 in Schedules 'A' and 'B' properties was held to be 3/5th, in Schedules 'C', and 'D' properties to be 1/5th and in Schedule 'D(1)' properties to be 4/15th. The share of defendant No. 2 in Schedules 'C' and 'D' properties was held to be 1/5th and in Schedule 'D(1)' properties to be 1/10th. The share of defendant No. 4 in Schedule 'D(1)' properties was held to be 1/3rd. 

 6. The preliminary decree drawn up on 27-3-73, however, did not reflect either the original or corrected order portion of the Judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge. It contained some mistakes with regard to the shares of the parties and remains uncorrected even to this day. 

 7. Mr. M. H. Khondkar, the learned Advocate for the appellant, in assailing the final decree submits that the preliminary decree having not been drawn up in accordance with the order portion of the Judgment there is no valid preliminary decree at all for effecting partition of the suit properties. The Pleader Commissioner could not have worked for effecting a partition of the suit properties in the absence of a validly drawn-up preliminary decree. There was no legal foundation for his work. His entire exercise was a nullity and the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in accepting his report. 

 8. Mr. Ghulam Rabbani, learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondents, submits, on the other hand, that notwithstanding some formal defects in the drawing up of the preliminary decree, the Pleader Commissioner while allocating sahams to the parties has not gone beyond the order portion of the judgment dated 28-2-73. The apportionment cannot be taken exception to and no party has received more or less than his or her share prescribed in the Judgment. Even if the decree were correctly drawn up the Pleader. Commissioner would have apportioned sahams to the parties exactly in the same proportion as he has done presently. Mr. Rabbani has submitted an application u/s. 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure, read with sections 151 & 153 thereof for correction of the preliminary decree and has submitted that the acceptance of the report of the Commissioner be upheld ex debito justiciae, in view of the fact that a clerical error of the Court should not be allowed to vitiate the entire proceedings specially when the error has not worked out to the prejudice of any party. 

 9. It appears that the Pleader Commissioner's report insofar as allocating sahams to the parties is concerned has not gone beyond the order portion of the learned Subordinate Judge's judgment dated 28-2-73. The question is, will the formal defects in the preliminary decree, which are clerical in nature, nullify the entire work of the Pleader Commissioner. 

 "It is settled that no litigant should be allowed to suffer through the mistake of any official of the Court who is connected with the administration of justice. Such mistakes can be corrected under sections 151 to 153, C.P.C. The Court has inherent power to rectify its own errors inadvertently committed and the language of s. 153 is wide enough to cover the correction of mistakes and errors in any proceeding in a suit." 

 In the case of Ahidhar Ghosh V. Secretary of State for India in Council, 36 CWN 665, a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court with Rankin, C.J. presiding held that where after the judgment of the High Court had been affirmed by the Privy Council the appellant discovered for the first time that in the High Court decree against him, the item of Court-fees paid by the other side on the memorandum of appeal to the High Court had been included twice in the costs, the High Court, on the application of such appellant, permitted the decree to be amended by debiting the costs overcharged. 

 12. We, therefore, hold that the Pleader Commissioner's report cannot be set aside on the ground that he lacked any jurisdictional basis for his work. His jurisdiction, under the circumstances is unaffected by the formal defects in the preliminary decree which can be corrected ex debito justiciae. 

 We shall dispose of the application for correction of the preliminary decree later. 

 13. Mr. M. H. Khondker has submitted next that the date 10.7.75 being fixed for filing of objection against the report of the Pleader Commissioner and not for consideration of the report or for hearing or disposal of the suit, the learned Subordinate Judge acted without jurisdiction in accepting the report of the Commissioner making partition of the property in suit without considering the same, in any manner and passing the final decree for partition. 

 "(3) Where the Court confirms or varies the report or reports it shall pass a decree in accordance with the same as confirmed or varied; but where the Court sets aside the report or reports it' shall either issue a new Commission or make such other order as it shall think fit." 

 In view of the provisions of Order 26, rule 14 (3) of the Code, Mr. Rabbani submits, no illegality, irregularity or mistake has been committed by the learned Subordinate Judge in passing a final decree on the date fixed for filing objection to the report, when no objection was filed and when there remained nothing for the Court but to proceed with the acceptance of the report and pass a final decree in accordance with the same. Order 26, rule 14 (3) of the Code, he submits, gives the learned Subordinate Judge full authority to act the way he has done in the present case. 

 15. Technically, Mr Rabbani's submission is unexceptionable, but from the facts and circumstances of the case it appear that there is more than mere technicality involved in it. The preliminary decree was passed on 28.2.7.3 and the Pleader Commissioner was appointed on 18.9.73. Nearly two years there after the Pleader Commissioner submitted his report. By Order No. 77 dated 10.6.75 the trial Court fixed 10.7.75 as the date for filing objection to the report of the Commissioner. The original order-sheet of the trial Court does not show that the recommencement in the Court of the proceedings of the partition suit on 10.6.75 after a lapse of more than one year, the last order of the trial Court being dated 4.6.74, was communicated to the plaintiff or the defendants or their respective lawyers. True, there is nothing in the Code of Civil Procedure or in Civil Rules & Order requiring the trial Court to intimate the parties of the recommencement of the proceedings, as a partition suit continues till the final decree is passed. It is the uniform practice of the Court; however, to inform the lawyers of parties when the Pleader Commissioner submits his report and when a date is fixed for filing objection to the same unless the parties or their respective lawyers are already informed about it. No intimation has been given to the lawyers of any side. Plaintiffs were aware of the recommencement of the proceedings in the trial Court, but the defendant No. 1 appellant says that he was not aware of it. Plaintiffs allege that the appellant watched the Courts cause list and the allegation of lack of knowledge is a deliberate attempt to delay the partition. It appears, however, that, since the Court's proceedings were not continuous and since the Court proceeded to pass the Order No. 77 dated 10.9.75 after an interval of one year without prior or subsequent notice to the lawyers of the, parties, there remains a reasonable possibility of missing the list. Under such circumstances we cannot shut our eyes to the fact that passing of the final decree on 10.7.75 has really been made without the appellant being given an opportunity to present his case against the report of the Pleader Commissioner. 

 17. In this case, too, there is no specific provision of serving notice upon the parties or their respective lawyers after the Pleader Commissioner submits his report. But if considerable time has elapsed between the last occasion when the court had dealt with the proceedings and the submission of the report, it is only fit and proper and, indeed, there is a practice that the lawyers of both sides are to be informed of the recommencement of the Court's proceedings. The decree passed without such intimation will not be a nullity, but in the facts and circumstances of each case the aggrieved party can complain about lack of knowledge of the last leg of proceedings and the Court would be required to examine if the complaint is a reasonable one. 

 18. Considering, therefore, the facts and circumstance of the case we hold that the acceptance of Commissioner's Report and passing of the final decree dated 10.7.75 cannot be maintained. The application for correction of the preliminary decree should be considered by the trial Court and the preliminary decree should be corrected. 

 20. In the result, P.A . No 15 of 1977 is allowed without any order as to costs. Order No. 78 dated 10.7.75 passed by learned subordinate Judge is set aside in its entirety. The learned subordinate Judge is directed to intimate the lawyers of the parties of the arrival of the records of the case and to fix another date for filing of objection against the report of the Pleader Commissioner and is further directed to complete the proceedings by passing a final decree within 3 (three) months from the arrival of the records of the case.
